headline: Henry Randall, president of the American Society of Transplant Surgeons, cautions against using AI blindly to decide who gets donor organs.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: fresh and read in full; it is one surgeon's view in an interview.
importance_line: People waiting for transplants depend on fair organ matching, which transplant surgeons and AI developers are looking to improve, but Randall's caution is one surgeon's view and he sits on the advisory board of a company building such tools.
summary: Healthcare Brew reports that Henry Randall, president of the American Society of Transplant Surgeons and a member of the advisory board of the AI company Valiant AI, said in an interview that AI cannot be fully relied on and that rushing it into use before there is education and engineering around it is not the way to approach it, even as companies and universities develop AI tools to help match donor organs to patients. To Randall's knowledge, no health system is using AI to predict outcomes and allocate organs outside research.
